# Independent audit: centroid defects with zero endpoint reserve



Source: `candidate 584edae5c582b753`.
Verifier: `supporting computation verify_zero_endpoint_reserve_centroid_defects_coherent.py`.


reran the latter successfully: **2057 exact checks**. The verifier uses
only rational arithmetic. The geometric completeness and compatibility
arguments below were checked separately from those computations.

## 1. Actual fibers and the endpoint support test

The convex hull over bases 0,1,2 has exactly the prescribed fibers
whenever (K_0+K_2)/2 is contained in K_1. At base 1 an arbitrary convex
combination assigns equal total weights to bases 0 and 2, with the
remaining weight on base 1. Convexity of K_1 then proves that the hull
adds no points to its fiber. The endpoint fibers are unchanged because
their bases are extreme. The projection is [0,2], so no other integer
fibers occur. Positive-dimensional endpoint bodies also ensure that
the ambient hull is full-dimensional.

If L_0 contains K_0 and is feasible with the other fibers fixed, its
midpoint with K_2 lies in K_1. Therefore, for every endpoint facet
normal r whose support is unchanged from A=(K_0+K_2)/2,

    h_L0(r) <= 2h_K1(r)-h_K2(r) = h_K0(r).

All facet inequalities force L_0 to lie in K_0. The other endpoint is
identical. This proves that no proper compact monotone enlargement is
possible. It also proves literal equality of the reserve polyhedron
with the endpoint: if the reserve contained any outside point, the
convex hull of that point with K_0 would be a feasible compact proper
enlargement by the exact reserve theorem. Thus the source does not
confuse absence of a particular facet motion with zero total reserve.

## 2. Planar example

The displayed pentagon is exactly (T+Q)/2. Every sum of vertices lies
in its inequalities, while each pentagon vertex has the stated
vertex-sum realization. The affine interpolation description at every
real base z is also correct: with s=z/2, the body
(1-s)T+sQ has vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,s),(s,1),(0,1),
with coincident vertices allowed at s=0 or 1.

Deleting the upper-right triangle from the unit square gives area
7/8 and coordinate moment 19/48, hence centroid coordinate 19/42.
Subtracting the endpoint centroid average 5/12 gives 1/28 in each
coordinate. Endpoint/middle areas are 1/2,7/8,1, total 19/8, and
every area is strictly less than total/2=19/16.

Here the middle fiber is precisely the Minkowski midpoint, so no
inclusion surplus contributes to the centroid defect. The midpoint
support equality holds in every direction and in particular at every
endpoint facet normal, locking both endpoint reserves. The positive
Brunn--Minkowski root deficit is consistent with the nonhomothetic
triangle and square; it does not contradict the support lock.

## 3. Spatial facet enumeration and support certificate

The six generators span R^3. For any normal r, the exposed face of
their zonotope is a translation of the zonotope generated by exactly
those generators orthogonal to r. Its dimension is the dimension of
their span. Every facet therefore contains two independent zero-dot
generators, and its normal is parallel to their cross product.
Conversely every nonzero pairwise cross product makes those two
independent generators free and exposes a two-dimensional facet.
Consequently the two signs of the fifteen listed cross products give
every facet, even though several are repetitions. There is no missing
facet classification assumption in this enumeration.

All fifteen exact scaled support slacks agree with the displayed
table, in lexicographic pair order:

    24000, 249900, 2400, -1010, 249900,
    300000, 24000, 30000, 252400, 274900,
    300000, 24990, 1490, 280160, 249899.

Since the zonotope is centrally symmetric, testing h_A(r)-|r.v|
tests both facet signs. The only negative entry is pair 15. Its
cross product is u=(0,-1/10,1), and its positive sign is the violated
one; u.v-h_A(u)=101/100000. The opposite sign is satisfied strictly.
Every other listed facet inequality is strictly satisfied at v.

The zero generators for u are precisely g_1 and g_5. The signs of
the other four are minus, plus, minus, plus, giving the fixed endpoint
sum c=(-9/40,-11/40,1/2). Thus the stated parallelogram F is exactly
the visible facet, not merely a subset of it.

## 4. Added pyramid, zonotope volume, and centroid

Because v satisfies all other facet inequalities, a segment from v
to any point of A enters A through F. Thus the outside part of
conv(A,v) is exactly the pyramid over F, up to null boundary pieces.
Conversely its open pyramid lies beyond the u facet and satisfies
the other inequalities. This justifies using one pyramid rather than
summing potentially overlapping additions.

Its side vectors are g_1/2 and g_5/2. The apex displacement from the
base centroid is epsilon u, so determinant/3 gives volume
101/1200000. The centroid of a three-dimensional pyramid is
(3c+v)/4. The displayed coordinate vector and its dot product
211101/400000 with u are correct.

The zonotope volume formula uses segments [0,g_i/2] after translation,
so its factor is exactly 1/8. The twenty absolute determinant
numerators listed in the source sum to 8631. Hence |A|=8631/8000.
The elementary segment-addition proof of that formula is valid:
every nonempty line fiber parallel to an added segment increases by
its length, and induction in dimension expands the projection area
into the required lower-dimensional determinants.

Since A is centrally symmetric its first moment vanishes. Adding
the pyramid therefore gives

    |K_1|=1294751/1200000,
    g(K_1)=(101/1294751) g_add != 0.

Both endpoints and the original midpoint A have centroid zero.
Thus this example's entire centroid midpoint defect is caused by
strict target inclusion, as claimed.

## 5. Endpoint locks and no-heavy condition

The endpoint K_0 facet normals are the cross products within the
first triple of generators, and those of K_2 are the cross products
within the last triple. The relevant table entries, including both
signs, are strictly positive. Therefore adding v changes none of
their midpoint support values, and Section 1 locks both reserves.
The one altered normal arises from generators in different endpoint
bodies. It is not an endpoint facet normal.

The determinant of the endpoint linear map is 1001/1000. The three
fiber volumes sum to 3695951/1200000, and their largest is
1294751/1200000. Its doubled numerator is 2589502, strictly below
3695951. Thus all three fibers are strictly below M/2, with two
occupied base parities. The example genuinely satisfies the stated
no-heavy condition.

## 6. Dimension padding and exact scope

Taking a common centered unit cube in additional continuous coordinates
preserves the old moments and all volume numbers. Product endpoint
facets consist of the old endpoint facets and the new coordinate
faces. The old normals remain locked; the new upper and lower support
values remain exactly the common cube values in both endpoint and
midpoint. All product facet inequalities therefore remain locked,
even for a proposed enlargement that couples old and new coordinates.

Taking a binary integer box adds no other integer bases. At a target
binary vertex, every anchored combination must stay at that vertex
in each binary coordinate, so the single-column endpoint lock still
applies. There are 3*2^(n-1) bases and 2^n occupied parities. Total mass
is multiplied by 2^(n-1), making M/k exactly the original single-column
M/2. The strict no-heavy property survives for every n>=1. These are
actual full-dimensional convex bodies in all asserted padded cases.

The conclusions concern independent monotone endpoint enlargement
with all other fibers fixed. They assert neither local depth minimality
nor the impossibility of joint or signed shape changes. They are exact
counterexamples to the proposed inference from a positive centroid
midpoint defect, including a pure inclusion defect, to available
independent endpoint reserve. This precise scope passes the audit.
